mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi engine typically costs between £2,200 and £3,500 for supply only, while used units start from around £450.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the FFDA and KKDA engine codes in the Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The FFDA code was used in the Mk1 Focus (2001-2004) and produces 100HP, while the KKDA code was introduced in the Mk2 (2004-2008) with an increased output of 115HP.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the torque-rich diesel alternative in the Focus range, the 1.8 TDCi variant evolved from the initial Mk1 Duratorq unit into a refined, higher-output engine for the Mk2 generation before being phased out in favour of the 1.6 and 2.0 TDCi units.

milestones.description: FFDA, 1.8L Diesel, 100HP (74kW) - Introduced in the Mk1 Focus, offering robust low-end torque for the Zetec, Ghia, and LX trims.
KKDA, 1.8L Diesel, 115HP (85kW) - Mk2 launch brought an updated Duratorq engine with improved injection and higher power output.
KKDB, 1.8L Diesel, 115HP (85kW) - Mk2.5 facelift update, featuring minor emissions and mapping refinements for the Titanium and Zetec S trims.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi is generally a robust Duratorq unit, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific wear points. The KKDA and KKDB codes dominate replacement demand for this variant due to turbo and EGR-related failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Clogging - Why the Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi (KKDA/KKDB) Restricts Airflow
problems.rootCause: Short urban journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles, while exhaust gases recirculated by the EGR valve deposit heavy carbon soot, restricting airflow and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and EGR maintenance.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage clogging, but does not fix underlying mechanical wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when carbon damage has caused secondary issues like turbo starvation or severe compression loss.

problems.recommendation: For most Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi owners, a specialist component repair (turbo refurbishment and injector seal replacement) offers the best financial return if the engine block is fundamentally sound. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic turbo debris ingestion or severe internal wear, sourcing a low-mileage used engine is often the most economically viable path, provided it comes with a verifiable warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Actuator & Injector Seal Failure - Why the Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi (FFDA/KKDA) Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbo actuator linkage seizes due to heat and carbon buildup, while aging injector copper seals allow combustion gases to escape, creating the infamous "black death" carbon crust around the injectors.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removing the turbo for refurbishment and replacing all injector seals.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the engine block and compression remain healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo failure has sent debris into the engine or if compression is compromised.

items.question: What are the common signs of Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.
keyPoints: A knocking sound from the top of the engine often indicates failing injector seals ("black death").
If the engine management light is flashing alongside these symptoms, stop driving immediately.
Continuing to drive can cause catastrophic internal damage to the engine block.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi?
items.answer: Given that Mk1 and Mk2 Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi models typically hold a market value between £800 and £3,500, a full rebuilt engine can cost more than the car is worth.
keyPoints: For most owners, sourcing a verified low-mileage used engine is the most financially sensible option.
Investing in targeted component repairs (like a turbo rebuild) is also viable if the engine block is healthy.
A rebuilt unit is only recommended if you plan to keep the vehicle long-term and it holds exceptional condition.

items.question: What is the difference between the FFDA and KKDA engine codes in the Ford Focus 1.8 TDCi?
items.answer: The FFDA code was used in the Mk1 Focus (2001-2004) and produces 100HP, while the KKDA code was introduced in the Mk2 (2004-2008) with an increased output of 115HP.
